history.dynasty: None (temple institution); founded by followers of the saint
history.period: 19th century (Swami Samarth lived at Akkalkot c. 1856-1878); present structures renovated 1920 and built 1943-1946
history.summary: The Akkalkot Swami Samarth Temple, officially the Shri Vatavruksha Swami Maharaj Devasthan, is the main shrine of Shri Swami Samarth Maharaj, the 19th-century saint revered as the fourth incarnation of Lord Dattatreya (and in some traditions the reincarnation of Narasimha Saraswati). Swami Samarth travelled across the subcontinent and settled at Akkalkot around 1856, living for over two decades mainly at the residence of his disciple Cholappa, under a banyan (vatavruksha) tree where he entered Mahasamadhi in 1878. Followers built a small temple around his samadhi; the complex has a two-storied building with a Nagarkhana, renovated in 1920, with the Sabha Mandap built in 1925 and the inner temple constructed 1943-1946. It houses his samadhi shrine, padukas and personal belongings (clothes, rosary, water pot), and is called Vatavruksha Mandir for the banyan tree. The trust runs a dharamshala, an Anna Chhatra serving free meals to pilgrims, a museum, a library and a meditation hall. It is one of the principal pilgrimage centres of the Datta Sampradaya, alongside Ganagapur, Narsobachi Wadi and Pithapuram.

name: Akkalkot Swami Samarth Temple
town_description: Akkalkot is a city and municipal council in Solapur district, Maharashtra, about 38 km southeast of Solapur and close to the Karnataka border. It was the capital of Akkalkot State, a princely state ruled by the Bhonsale dynasty during the British Raj (population ~40,103 in 2011). The city is best known as the home of Shri Swami Samarth Maharaj, the 19th-century saint believed to be an incarnation of Lord Dattatreya. Nearby attractions include the Akkalkot Fort and palace, the Shri Siddheshwar Temple at Solapur, and Naladurg Fort; the town is locally known for Shenga (peanut) chutney.

travel.airport: Pune International Airport (approx. 245-290 km) is the nearest major airport (verify - Solapur airport may have limited/regional services); taxi or bus onward to Akkalkot.
travel.railway: Akkalkot Road Railway Station (approx. 11 km); Solapur Junction (approx. 38-40 km) is the nearest major railhead with trains across India.
travel.road: About 38-40 km southeast of Solapur; well connected by road with buses and taxis from Solapur, Pune and Mumbai. MSRTC buses run from Solapur bus stand.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. The Punyatithi (Chaitra, March-April), Guru Purnima and Datta Jayanti draw very large crowds; weekdays are quieter for a peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM, with an afternoon break (verify - some sources list 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM. Kakad Aarti 5:00 AM, Shej Aarti approx. 8:00 PM). General darshan is free. The Shri Swami Samarth Anna Chhatra serves free meals to all pilgrims, typically during the afternoon closure (verify current meal timings). Dress modestly; photography generally restricted inside.
